questions.question: Bearing + housing for conveyors is called?
questions.explanation: Pillow block units combine a bearing and housing for easy bolting onto frames and conveyors.

questions.question: Which bearing self-aligns for shaft bending?
questions.explanation: Spherical roller bearings have a spherical outer raceway, allowing shaft misalignment.

questions.question: Linear guides are used for what?
questions.explanation: Linear guides give accurate, low-friction straight movement in machine tools and robots.

questions.question: Bearing suffix 'K' means?
questions.explanation: K means a 1:12 tapered bore, mounted with an adapter or withdrawal sleeve.

questions.question: Tapered bore bearings mount on shafts with?
questions.explanation: An adapter sleeve with lock nut fixes a tapered bore bearing on a plain shaft.

questions.question: Machine tool spindles need which bearings?
questions.explanation: Super precision angular contact bearings give spindles high speed and accuracy.

questions.question: Machined brass cages suit which duty?
questions.explanation: Machined brass cages are strong and resist the shock loads in screens and crushers.

questions.question: Cylindrical roller type 'NU' allows what?
questions.explanation: NU types have no ribs on the inner ring, so the shaft can move axially.

questions.question: Which bearing suits very heavy radial load?
questions.explanation: Line contact of cylindrical rollers gives high radial load capacity.

questions.question: Wind turbine main shafts often use?
questions.explanation: Large spherical or tapered roller bearings carry heavy main-shaft loads and misalignment.

questions.question: Which seal type has the lowest friction?
questions.explanation: Non-contact seals and shields don't rub the inner ring, so friction is lowest.

questions.question: Bearings in food plants often need?
questions.explanation: Food plants need corrosion-resistant stainless or coated bearings with food-grade grease.

questions.question: Kiln and crusher bearings are needed by?
questions.explanation: Cement plants run kilns, crushers, mills and fans with heavy-duty bearings.

questions.question: Rolling mills and casters are found in?
questions.explanation: Steel plants use large roller bearings in continuous casters and rolling mills.

questions.question: Sugar mill bearing demand peaks before?
questions.explanation: Mills run hard during cane crushing, so maintenance buys bearings before it starts.

questions.question: Railway axle boxes commonly use?
questions.explanation: Railway axles use tapered (often cartridge) or cylindrical roller bearings.

questions.question: Textile spindles need bearings that are?
questions.explanation: Textile machines run many spindles at speed, needing quiet, low-friction bearings.

questions.question: Paper machine dryer bearings face what?
questions.explanation: Steam-heated dryer cylinders run hot, so bearings need heat-stable steel and oil.

questions.question: Electric motors and pumps mostly use?
questions.explanation: Deep groove ball bearings are the standard choice in electric motors and pumps.

questions.question: Mining vibrating screens need bearings with?
questions.explanation: Screens shake at high g-forces, so bearings with robust cages are used.

questions.question: Industrial distributors mainly sell to?
questions.explanation: Authorised distributors serve maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) buyers locally.

questions.question: Fake bearings are risky because they?
questions.explanation: Counterfeits use poor steel and heat treatment, causing early failure and safety risks.

questions.question: Genuine NSK bearings should be bought from?
questions.explanation: Authorised distributors source directly from NSK, avoiding counterfeit risk.

questions.question: Channel stuffing means what?
questions.explanation: Pushing more stock than dealers can sell inflates sales briefly but hurts later.

questions.question: 'Sell-out' means sales made by?
questions.explanation: Sell-out tracks real end-user demand, unlike sell-in from NSK to the distributor.

questions.question: Distributor stock health is shown by?
questions.explanation: Higher inventory turns mean stock is moving and the dealer's cash is not stuck.

questions.question: Best tool to mount small bearings?
questions.explanation: Induction heaters expand the inner ring evenly; hammers and flames damage bearings.

questions.question: Never heat a bearing above about?
questions.explanation: Heating above about 120 °C can change the hardness and dimensions of bearing steel.

questions.question: Main cause of early bearing failure?
questions.explanation: Poor or contaminated lubrication causes a large share of early bearing failures.

questions.question: Root cause failure analysis helps users?
questions.explanation: RCFA finds why bearings fail so the fix prevents costly repeat breakdowns.

questions.question: Common bearing condition monitoring tool?
questions.explanation: Vibration and temperature trends warn of damage long before breakdown.

questions.question: Shaft alignment is best done with?
questions.explanation: Laser tools align shafts precisely, cutting bearing loads and vibration.

questions.question: Too much grease in a bearing causes?
questions.explanation: Excess grease churns, raising temperature and damaging seals.

questions.question: Preferred tool to remove a bearing?
questions.explanation: Pullers apply force evenly to remove bearings without damaging the shaft.

questions.question: Premium bearing value is shown by lower?
questions.explanation: Lower Total Cost of Ownership from longer life and less downtime justifies a premium.

questions.question: Downtime cost vs bearing price is often?
questions.explanation: One unplanned stop can cost far more than the bearing, so reliability sells.

questions.question: Sealed bearings save users money by?
questions.explanation: Sealed, greased-for-life units cut maintenance labour and contamination failures.

questions.question: Energy-saving bearings reduce what?
questions.explanation: Lower friction means less power consumed by motors, fans and pumps.

questions.question: Life cycle cost = price + energy + ?
questions.explanation: Life cycle cost adds purchase, installation, energy, maintenance and downtime costs.

questions.question: First step before quoting an industrial user?
questions.explanation: Learning the application, load, speed and pain points leads to the right solution.

questions.question: CRM software stores what?
questions.explanation: CRM tracks customers, visits, opportunities and follow-ups for the sales team.

questions.question: Sales funnel stage right after a new lead?
questions.explanation: Leads are qualified for need, budget and timing before proposals are made.

questions.question: Actual sales ÷ target × 100 gives?
questions.explanation: Achievement % shows how much of the sales target was met in the period.

questions.question: A dealer credit limit controls what?
questions.explanation: Credit limits cap how much a dealer may owe, controlling bad-debt risk.

questions.question: Bad debt risk rises when DSO is?
questions.explanation: Long payment delays raise the chance of non-payment and lock up cash.

questions.question: NSK's technology slogan is Motion &?
questions.explanation: NSK aims to benefit society through its 'Motion & Control' technologies.
